title: Tropical cyclone‐induced estuarine destratification and protracted recovery
content:
Abstract

Estuarine stratification regulates nutrient cycling and ecosystem dynamics, yet its resilience to extreme meteorological events remains poorly understood. Here, we combine high-resolution observations and numerical modeling to capture the full-cycle physical response of an estuary to a summer typhoon. Results show that within 48 h, vigorous vertical mixing driven by typhoon wind stress erased salinity-driven stratification and homogenized the water column. A salinity budget reveals vertical mixing as the dominant destratification mechanism. Following the typhoon, the system entered a prolonged recovery exceeding 7 d, during which gradually re-established stratification. Notably, we document significant decoupling in recovery timescales: surface freshwater plume signatures began recovering within days, whereas bottom water property shifts lagged by ~ 6 d. This depth-dependent recovery underscores that estuarine restoration after extreme mixing is a multi-stage process. It improves understanding of estuarine stratification responding to and recovering from tropical cyclones, and highlights the importance of considering depth-dependent recovery processes when assessing post-storm estuarine conditions.
